image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey Flash Express parcel shop building, detailed front elevation with a glazed frontage and service counter at the window under a saturated yellow fascia carrying the black Flash Express wordmark and lightning device on a backlit sign, a yellow roller shutter box above the opening and parcel shelving visible inside, plain rendered side and rear walls with a wide roller loading shutter, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: yellow printed acrylic sign face and yellow painted panel at the front, plate glass, flat painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised shutter and roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: Flash Express. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93, up from 0.91. 3528/16000 triangles, 13/16 draw calls, 8/8 materials, 13/32 unique geometries, 5 textures at 8.7 MB. Every critical feature is at or above its threshold. The owner's seven items are all on the model: plain glass, a generated mark with no bolt/E overlap, an open hatch, square units at the back with no debris, a centred shutter under a flush box hood, textured plant, and wear on the lintel and hood with the counter clean. Residuals: the harness rig is not the plate's studio light, the render and wear tiles are procedural, and the plate's interior is by choice not shown.

featureReviews.evidence: Building envelope 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 4.6 x 7; the rooftop plant reaches 4.82 and the shutter hood reaches x 4.22, both inside the asset's 10% tolerance. Shopfront 6.80 m of the 8.00 m front, shutter 4.44 x 2.70 m centred on its wall, fascia 7.50 m, hatch 3.0 x 0.62 m -- every one read off the rectified elevation or set by the brief.
featureReviews.notes: Third build. The silhouette events the brief moved: both rooftop units stand square at the back of the roof with the duct kerb gone (the plate yaws one near the middle), and the shutter hood is a 0.50 m box flush with its guides standing 0.28 m proud of the wall rather than a 0.065 m lip oversailing them. What remains is the declaration: Meshy reads this plate 29% taller than the shared module, and the module wins.

featureReviews.evidence: Yellow lightbox #fff600 (PBR confidence 0.829) 7.50 m wide in a dark border standing proud of the parapet, carrying a nano-banana-2 generated FLASH EXPRESS mark -- black caps, WHITE black-outlined bolt for the S, EXPRESS right-aligned under the H with clear yellow before the bolt's tail -- cut out, snapped to the fascia yellow and placed at the measured u 0.233..0.626, v 0.157..0.882 of the 2048x320 band.
featureReviews.notes: The second build set the mark from a font by measured boxes and the bolt's tail ran through the E of EXPRESS, which is what the owner saw. The generated mark keeps the plate's layout and the letterforms are the brand's heavy oblique sans rather than DejaVu Bold stretched to fit. Placement is unchanged from the measurement, so nothing was re-judged by eye; the bolt tail is clipped flat at the generated image's bottom edge, which is the one residual.

featureReviews.evidence: Yellow jambs at X -3.51..-3.16 and +2.94..+3.29, a lintel cantilevering over the glazing at Y 2.70..3.19, and the counter worktop at 1.10..1.18 passing OUT through the open hatch on a downturned edge -- one material, one draw call. The lintel and jambs carry a dust-and-streak tile (patchAmp 26, streakAmp 26 at 2.0 m); every vertex in the counter's world box is pinned to a clean texel.
featureReviews.notes: Two brief items land here. The counter came DOWN from 1.40 to counter height, which is what opens the hatch above it; and the wear the plate shows on the lintel (grey grime along its top and streaking down the face) is on the model now, while the worktop is spotless because it samples one untouched texel rather than a cleaner region of the same tile. The tile is procedural, so the marks are the right kind and strength and not in the plate's own places.

featureReviews.evidence: Plain tinted plate glass, #6f8a8c at opacity 0.90 / roughness 0.12, over a dark backdrop slab folded into the roof-deck submission by vertex tone. The hatch is a real 3.0 x 0.62 m gap between the middle bay's two panels with its own head rail at 1.72, and the transom rail stops either side of the bay. Measured at azimuth 0: glass luma 141, hatch 74, backdrop 58.
featureReviews.notes: Replaces the second build's projected interior, which the owner rejected. The first backdrop tone (0x606060) rendered the hatch near black -- a hole to the gate and to a viewer -- and 0x9a9a9a puts it at 74, dark enough to read as an opening beside the 141 glass and clear of the backdrop band. Scored 0.90 and not higher because the plate does show an interior and the model, by the brief, shows a dim room and a counter edge.

featureReviews.evidence: 40 half-round beads at 62 mm pitch over a 4.44 x 2.70 m opening at Z -2.37..+2.07, centred on the +X wall, between two guide channels, over a bottom rail and under a 0.50 m hood flush with the guides' outer faces and 0.28 m proud of the wall. Galvanised spangle tile at 1.4 m over beads and guides; galv albedo #d8dfe5 = #b6bcc1 / the tile's 0.841 mean multiplier.
featureReviews.notes: Width and pitch are the plate's measurements; the placement is the brief's (the plate has the opening 0.46 m toward the front). The hood was the visible defect: a thin lip 0.44 m longer than the guides, reading as an overhang past the door. It is now the plate's box hood, and the grime tile on the cast stone puts the streaking the owner named on it.

featureReviews.evidence: Two packaged units, 1.34 x 0.90 x 0.88 m, both square to the building at x +-1.50, z -2.05, one instanced geometry: casing in the generated galvanised spangle, the grille's back plate 0x4a4e52 and fan disc 0x3c4044 behind blades at 0xa8acb0 by vertex colour, flanged lid, cowl, seams and feet. The duct kerb between them is gone.
featureReviews.notes: The owner named three things -- one unit yawed, debris beside it, both to go to the back -- and a fourth, that the casings looked flat. The yaw and the kerb were the plate's, and the brief overrides them. The texture is nano-banana-2's galvanised sheet, contrast halved so it reads as zinc mottle rather than marble (the first normalisation clipped 40% of the spangle to white), and the dark tone behind the blades is what finally makes the grille read as an intake instead of a panel of the casing. The units still overrun the declared height by 0.22 m, inside tolerance and deliberate.

featureReviews.evidence: A real leaf on a real hinge at the RIGHT jamb (X +2.89), 1.36 x 2.11 m, with stiles, rails, a plain glazed pane and a vertical pull bar on two stand-offs at X +1.83.
featureReviews.notes: Unchanged apart from the pane, which is now plain glass like the fixed glazing. Hung on the right because the plate's handle plate is on the LEFT of the leaf, the leading edge of a right-hung door. The ONE thing on this prop that moves and the only named pivot beyond the root.

featureReviews.evidence: Pale cast stone (#a9adb1, PBR confidence 0.726) capping front, sides and rear at ONE level, y 4.44..4.60, inset from the parapet faces; the 0.50 m shutter hood flush with the guides; the plinth under the shopfront. One submission, carrying a grime-and-streak tile at 1.6 m.
featureReviews.notes: Grouped by MATERIAL rather than location. The hood's grime is what the brief asked for on the 'silver overhang'; the coping ring takes the same tile, which is where a real coping's streaking starts.

featureReviews.evidence: A seamless 512 tile in MULTIPLIER space -- rain streaking off the coping, patchy float marks, board-marked seams at 1.2 m and fine aggregate speckle -- repeated metrically at 3.2 m over the shell and the parapet. Lit front wall luma 193 against the plate's 193.
featureReviews.notes: Unchanged from the second build. Procedural, so the marks are the right kind and strength and not in the plate's own places.

notes: Built on the shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m building module: detailed front elevation, plain rendered side and rear walls, no loose objects outside. Saturated yellow livery with the black wordmark and a WHITE lightning device with a black outline. Shopfront centred on the facade, with a hinged entrance door (door-hinge pivot) on the right and a yellow delivery counter with a small hatch opening in the glazing on the left. The rear roller loading shutter is part of the building, not a separate object.
